messages:
Alex K: quick one — proposing a small "feature lookup" endpoint for the API so clients can ask what a model supports and its limits. e.g. when you hit a model id, it returns supported surfaces and token caps. helpful for SDKs and UI.
Maria T: +1. helps avoid magic client-side heuristics. rough shape I sketched:
Maria T: ```json
{
  \"model\": \"redwood-3b\",
  \"surfaces\": [\"chat\", \"embeddings\", \"rerank\"],
  \"supports_streaming\": true,
  \"supports_tool_calls\": true,
  \"structured_output\": { \"json_schema\": true },
  \"tool_whitelist\": [\"kb-search\", \"code-exec\"],
  \"max_request_tokens\": 4096,
  \"max_context_tokens\": 8192,
  \"embedding_dim\": 1536
}
```
Maria T: fields are suggestions — we should standardize names.
Devon R: a few questions:
Devon R: 1) do we expose per-route limits (chat vs embed) or just model-level? customers care about per-surface caps.
Devon R: 2) how do we express degraded behaviors (e.g., streaming available but only for < 2048 tokens)?
Priya S: for rollout/launch criteria we need:
Priya S: - spec doc + example SDK usage
Priya S: - sample client-side UI (dropdown that greys out unsupported features)
Priya S: - integration tests (embedding dims, rerank score shape, tool proxy auth)
Priya S: - perf SLO targets (95th < 120ms for small chat, embedding batch throughput target)
Alex K: I'd start with model-level caps and a per-surface optional override map. simpler for MVP.
Alex K: on expressing degraded features we can use a small enum: \"supported\", \"limited\", \"unsupported\" and add a details object when \"limited\".
Maria T: example diff for limited:
Maria T: ```json
{ \"streaming\": \"limited\", \"streaming_details\": \"streaming only for requests < 2048 tokens\" }
```
Devon R: sounds good. also need to include auth scope for tool_calls (so client UI can hide buttons if not permitted).
Priya S: launch checklist additions: docs + changelog, discover endpoint in the hosted API, SDK adapter in node/python, telemetry events (feature_probe_ok / feature_probe_mismatch), and a migration note for existing clients.
Alex K: backward-compat note: if the endpoint is missing for some model, SDK should assume a conservative default (no streaming, 4096 tokens).
InfraBot: DeployBot: feature-prober v1 deployed to staging :white_check_mark:
Devon R: can infra put a small table in the console listing models and their main flags? product can iterate on UI later.
Maria T: yes — we can expose the endpoint and add a lightweight UI later. also we should version the response (\"schema_version\": \"2026-03-01\") so we can extend.
Priya S: final ask from customers we've heard: explicit rerank contract (score range, tie-break deterministic) and embedding dims included. call that out in the spec.
Alex K: agree. I'll draft a short spec doc + proto for the endpoint and link to SDK examples. keeping launch scope: model-level flags + per-surface optional overrides, enum for limited states, tool whitelist + auth scope, embedding_dim, token caps, and schema_version.
Maria T: 👍 please ping #devex when ready for SDK review.
Alex K: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
